post.caption:
One night of restricted sleep raises ghrelin, the hormone that says eat, and lowers leptin, the one that says stop. Both controls pushed the wrong way before you have made a single decision. Cravings skew towards high-calorie food because a tired brain wants fast energy, and insulin sensitivity measurably drops after even short-term restriction. Which means sleep is not just a rest intervention. It is a metabolic one.
